p.seg: Principles:
To commend the worthy and revere virtue
casts a lasting light for a thousand years;
to honor the root and respect beginnings
naturally extends the meaning far and wide.
King Yuán of Chǔ accumulated benevolence and laid the foundation of virtue,
opening up this territory;
his virtuous customs and moral achievements
set an example for future generations.
The prosperity of his lineage
Shí Lóng 實隆 despised his ancestors;
the fragrance and glory they left behind
flourished for a hundred generations.
Yet their mounds and tombs are overgrown,
and their graves are untended.
Thinking of the distant past,
I am filled with enduring sorrow.
It is said that in loving a person, one loves the tree;
even the sweet pear tree should not be cut down.
In pursuing and recognizing ruined tombs,
even the memory of Xìn Líng 信陵 should not be forgotten.
How much more so for that which is the origin of continuous growth,
where the source of prosperity begins!
Let five households near the tomb be exempted from labor
and permanently assigned to sweep and clean it.
This may be implemented accordingly.
This is what is meant by the Shāng sound, with the five notes complete.
*Jī Shūyè*'s Preface to the Rhapsody on the Qin
When I was young, I loved music and sound,
and when I grew up, I delighted in it.
I believed that things have their rise and decline,
but this has no change;
flavors can become tiresome,
but this does not weary.
That which can guide and nurture the spirit and qi,
express and harmonize emotions and aspirations,
and prevent one from being depressed when in distress and alone,
nothing is closer than music and sound.
Therefore, if repetition is not enough,
then one chants and sings to give vent to one's aspirations;
if chanting and singing are not enough,
then one uses words to broaden one's meaning.
However, the instruments of the eight tones
and the forms of song and dance,
talented scholars throughout the ages
have all composed rhapsodies and eulogies for them.
Their style and spirit
have all been copied from each other.
When praising their materials,
they consider the precarious and difficult to be the best;
when describing their sounds,
they consider sadness to be the main theme;
when extolling their influence,
they consider shedding tears to be precious.
It is beautiful, indeed beautiful,
but still it does not fully comprehend the principle.
Investigating the reason for this,
it seems originally he didn't understand sounds,
examining its purpose,
he also didn't grasp the emotions of ritual and music.
Among all instruments,
the qín's 琴 virtue is the most excellent,
therefore, I compile and narrate my feelings,
to create a *fù* 賦 for it.
The *cí* 辭 says:
Oh, it grows where the *yǐwú* 椅梧 grows,
Relying on the lofty ridges of the high mountains.
Unveiling layers of soil to be born and carried,
Measuring the stars and reaching the highest dignity.
Containing the pure harmony of heaven and earth,
Absorbing the auspicious light of the sun and moon.
Flourishing uniquely in dense profusion,
Sending brilliant blossoms into the vast blue sky.
In the evening, it takes its image from the *Yúyuān* 虞淵,
At dawn, it dries its trunk in the nine *yáng* 陽 realms.
Waiting for its value for a thousand years,
Remaining silently divine, abiding in eternal peace.
Moreover, its mountain and river terrain,
is winding and hidden deep,
rocky, precipitous, and craggy.
Hù Lǐng's precipitous cliffs,
are rugged and craggy.
Red cliffs are dangerous and steep,
blue walls ten thousand *xún* high.
If indeed multiple peaks rise higher,
reclining and towering, clouds covering them,
far-reaching, lofty, supremely magnificent,
rising loftily, extraordinarily beautiful.
They steam spiritual essence to scatter clouds,
and based on divine depths, spout torrents.
Then the billows rush and surge,
madly racing, contending to flow.
They strike rocks and crash against corners,
their pent-up anger violently bursting forth.
Rushing and surging,
snatching foam and tossing waves.
Gushing and roaring,
coiling like snakes intertwined.
They unrestrainedly flow into the great rivers,
and succor the central lands (*Zhōngzhōu*).
Calmly circling and slowly advancing,
silently and continually floating.
Calmly expansive,
winding around mountains and hills.
Carefully observing the land's produce and nurture,
the treasures and resources that the depths protect.
Precious and strange *lánggān* coral,
beautiful *yáojǐn* jades, bright red.
Gathered and accumulated,
spreading out profusely on its sides.
As for spring orchids covering its east side,
and *shātáng* trees planted on its west.
Juānzǐ resides on its south-facing slope,
and jade-like sweet wine springs forth in front.
Dark clouds shade its top,
and soaring *luán* birds gather on its peak.
Clear dew moistens its surface,
and gentle breezes flow in its midst.
Tall and solemn in its stillness,
densely subtle in its tranquility.
The reason for arranging its surroundings
is indeed because of its naturally divine beauty,
sufficient to inspire thought, desire, love, and joy.
Thereupon, hermits,
companions of Róng Qī and Qǐ Jì,
then ascend the flying bridges together,
cross the secluded ravines,
grasp the jade branches,
and climb the steep cliffs,
to wander at its base.
Circling around and gazing afar,
they seem to be soaring in flight.
Slanting their eyes towards the Kūnlún Mountains,
looking down upon the seashores.
Pointing to the distant and far-reaching Cāngwú,
He arrived at the majestic beauty of the Huí River.
He realized the many burdens of worldly customs,
And looked up to the remaining radiance of Mount Jī.
He admired the vast openness of this mountain,
And, filled with enthusiasm, forgot about returning home.
His emotions were released in distant vistas,
Connecting with the legacy of Xuānyuán.
He admired Lǎo Tóng in the corner of Guī,
And revered Tài Róng's lofty chants.
Looking at this *wú* tree, he became thoughtful,
Contemplating borrowing an object to entrust his heart.
So he cut off branches of the *sūn* tree,
Measuring and considering what it could bear.
A man of utmost wisdom expressed his thoughts,
Creating a refined *qín*.
Thereupon he had Lí Zǐ oversee the inking,
And the master craftsman Shí wield the axe.
Kuí and Xiāng offered their methods,
Bān and Chuí exerted their divine skills.
Carving the joints and arranging recesses,
Open and close, adjusting to harmony.
Splendid paintings and carvings,
Arranging patterns and displaying designs.
Inlaid with rhinoceros horn and ivory,
Adorned with emerald green.
Stringed with the silk of the gardener,
Marked with jade from Zhōng Mountain.
Here are images of dragons and phoenixes,
and forms of ancient people.
Bó Yá waves his hand,
Zhōng Qī listens to the sound.
The appearance is bright and shining,
emitting brilliance and spreading light.
How beautiful it is!
Líng Lún compares the pitch pipes,
Tián Lián holds the zither.
Presented to the sovereign,
the new sound is clear and bright.
How magnificent it is!
When it is first tuned,
the *jiao* and *yu* notes both rise,
the *gōng* and *zhǐ* notes correspond and prove each other.
Varied sounds emanate together,
and the upper and lower parts respond in layers.
With stumbling and bumpy sounds,
a beautiful sound is about to emerge.
It is truly harmonious and pleasing enough to indulge in.
Then, one arranges the correct sounds,
and plays wondrous melodies.
Raising "White Snow,"
emitting the clear *jiao* note.
It scatters and spreads in a flowing manner,
luxuriously abundant and rich.
Brilliantly sparkling and soaring high,
Dangers follow close upon each other.
The rushing sounds surge and compete,
blossoming and shining with elaborate beauty.
It resembles towering mountains,
and also images flowing waves.
Vast and surging,
dense and lofty.
Restless and pent-up anxieties,
winding and leisurely dances.
Mounting high and scattering freely,
rapidly displaying abundant splendor.
Restraining appearance and giving measure,
responding to changes with fitting control.
Competing for fame and excelling in profession,
safely following the path and proceeding slowly.
Abundant and harmonious,
the sound and fame spread far and wide.
Containing manifest beauty to the end,
floating lingering echoes into the great void.
As for high-roofed flying pavilions,
spacious halls and quiet rooms;
on a solemn and clear winter night,
the bright moon casts its light.
New clothes are emerald-bright,
and cap-strings flow with fragrance.
Then, instruments are cool, strings are tuned,
the mind is at ease, and the hand is nimble.
The touch of the plectrum responds as intended,
Suí yì suǒ nǐ. (Following only the intention's conception.)
Chū shè lù shuǐ, (Initially venturing into the green waters,)
zhōng zòu qīng zhǐ. (Midway presenting a clear zhǐ [musical mode].)
Yǎ chǎng Táng Yáo, (Elegantly prolonging [the praise of] Táng Yáo,)

Kuān míng hóng rùn, (Broad and bright, vast and enriching,)

Fǔ xián ān gē, (Strumming the strings and peacefully singing,)

Gē yuē: (The song says:)
"Líng fú yáo xī qì yíng zhōu, (I ride the whirlwind to rest on Yingzhou,)
yào Liè Zǐ xī wèi hǎo chóu. (I invite Liè Zǐ to be my good companion.)
Cān hàng xiè xī dài zhāo xiá, (I dine on dew and wear the morning mist,)
miǎo piān piān xī bó tiān yóu. (Lightly soaring, I travel near the heavens.)
Qí wàn wù xī chāo zì dé, (Treating all things equally, I surpass self-possession,)
wěi xìng mìng xī rèn qù liú. (Entrusting fate, I let it decide when to go and stay.)
Jī qīng xiǎng yǐ fù huì, (Arousing clear sounds to attend the gathering,)
hé xián gē zhī chóu miù!" (Why be so anxious about stringed songs!)"
Yú shì qǔ yǐn xiàng lán, (Thereupon, as the melody gradually approached its end,)
zhòng yīn jiāng xiē. (The various sounds were about to cease.)
Gǎi yùn yì diào, (Changing the rhymes and shifting the key,)

Yáng hé yán, (Raising gentle smiles,)
rǎng hào wàn, (Baring pale wrists,)
fēi xiān zhǐ yǐ chí wù, (Delicate fingers flew and galloped,)

Constrained, stifled, suppressed.
Revolving, nurturing,
Calmly, secretly, enjoyed.
Suddenly bursting forth,
Wind-startled, cloud-disordered.
Desolate, severe,
Spreading out, half scattered.
Abundant, diffuse,
Elegant, resplendent, brilliantly radiant.
Excellent sounds emanate forth,
Abundant, bright and clear.
Sometimes mixed sounds are confused,
Appearing like strange pursuits.
Two beauties advance together,
Running abreast, with wings driving them on.
Initially as if about to diverge,
Ultimately converging on the same goal.
Sometimes curved but not yielding,
Straight but not arrogant.
Sometimes encroaching without chaos,
Sometimes separated without disparity.
At times seizing and constraining with fervor,
Or resentful and hesitant.
Suddenly drifting lightly and freely,
Suddenly lingering, connected and luxuriant.
Sometimes intermingling, dense and urgent,
Repeated, piled up, crowded and narrow.
Horizontal and vertical, continuous,
Dashing and fleeing, pressing each other.
Patting and sighing, repeatedly praising,
with no room for respite.
Rare, beautiful, and extraordinary,
impossible to fully describe.
Then there is the leisurely, elegant, and refined,
both grand and delicate, each appropriate.
Clear and harmonious, extended and smooth,
subtle variations, luxuriant and distinct.
Serene and gentle, bringing joy,
compliant and docile, flowing and sinuous.
Sometimes seizing opportune moments,
taking advantage of gaps, approaching danger.
Warbling like a departing *kun* bird singing in a clear pond,
its wings like a migrating swan soaring among layered cliffs.
Flourishing patterns ripple and spread,
like garments, sparse and disheveled.
Faint breeze, lingering sound,
gently undulating, beautiful and flowing.
Sometimes embracing, grasping, tickling, and stroking,
ethereal, swirling, scattered, and crisp.
Lightly moving and floating,
clear strokes, clever and wise.
Swift but not rushed,
lingering but not stagnant.
Fluttering, continuous, floating and distant,
a faint sound quickly passing away.
Listening to it from afar,
it is as if luán fèng and heron-phoenix are harmonizing and singing playfully in the clouds;
examining it closely,
it is as if numerous blossoms are spreading their splendor in the radiant spring breeze.
It is both abundant and rich in varied forms,
and also begins well and ends excellently.
Alas, its beauty and magnificence,
how boundless are its transformations!
As for the beginning of the third month of spring,
with beautiful attire appropriate to the season.
Then one brings along friends,
to wander and play.
Traversing the orchid garden,
ascending the layered foundation.
With the long forest behind,
shaded by flowery zhī (芝, a type of fungus believed to have medicinal properties).
Beside the clear stream,
composing new poems.
Praising the carefree joy of the fine fish and dragons,
delighting in the flourishing abundance of the hundred herbs.
Playing the surviving tune of Chóng Huá (重華, another name for Emperor Shun),
filled with longing and lengthy contemplation of distant admiration.
As for elegant hall banquets,
close friends and near guests are present.
Orchid delicacies are served alongside imperial fare,
and the fine wine is clear and pure.
Entering *Nán Jīng*,
originating from *Xī Qín*.
Continuing *Shào Língyáng*,
influencing the *Bā* people.
Variations in application arise together in complexity,
startling the masses and astonishing the spirits.
Assessing diverse merits to compare the playing,
how could the *shēng* and *yuè* instruments be comparable?
If we were to list the tunes and their suitable introductions,

*Wáng Zhāo* and the *Chǔ* concubine,

However, one who is not broad and far-reaching,
cannot frolic and play with it;
one who is not profound and tranquil,
cannot rest and be still with it;
Only those who are unrestrained and open-minded
can truly appreciate its unconstrained nature;
only those who are extremely refined
can analyze its principles.
If we discuss its structure and momentum,
and examine its style and sound,
when the instrument is harmonious, the resonance is free;
when the strings are tightly stretched, the sound is clear.
When the spacing is wide, the tone is low;
when the strings are long, the harmonics ring out.
Its nature is pure, tranquil, upright, and orderly,
containing the peace and harmony of the highest virtue.
Truly, it can move and stir the heart and mind,
and express hidden emotions.
Therefore, those who harbor sorrow, upon hearing it,
cannot help but feel sorrowful, grieved, and miserable,
with a mournful expression and a wounded heart.
Filled with grief and sighing,
they cannot restrain themselves.
Those who are healthy and happy, upon hearing it,
are joyful, cheerful, and relieved,
clapping, dancing, and overflowing with exuberance.
Lingering and indulging,
laughing and joking all day long.
If those who are peaceful listen to it,
they are nourished and delighted,
becoming virtuous, reverent, profound, and genuine.
Find joy in tranquility and emptiness, delight in antiquity,
Abandon affairs and forget oneself.
Therefore, Bó Yí 伯夷 used it to be incorruptible,
Yán Huí 顏回 used it to be benevolent,
Bǐ Gān 比干 used it to be loyal,
Wěi Shēng 尾生 used it to be trustworthy.
Huì Shī 惠施 used it to be eloquent and quick-witted,
Wàn Shí 萬石 used it to be taciturn and cautious.
The rest extend in kind,
What they achieve is not the same.
They arrive at the same destination by different paths,
Some refined, some simple.
Embracing the mean and harmony to govern all things,
All are used daily without error.
Its ability to move people and animals,
Is truly great!
At that time,
Metal and stone musical instruments silenced their sounds,
Gourds and bamboo wind instruments held their breath.
Wáng Bào 王豹 stopped singing,
Dí Yá 狄牙 lost his sense of taste.
Tiān Wú 天吳 leapt for joy in the deep abyss,

The wǔ yuè zhuó 舞鸑鷟 danced on the courtyard steps,
The wandering maidens fluttered and gathered.
It moves Heaven and Earth to achieve harmony,
How much more so the crawling multitude.
Appreciating the excellence and abundance of this instrument,
I sing of this composition to console myself.
Forever using and enjoying it without weariness,
Truly this is what both the ancients and the present cherish.
Final stanza:
Deep and serene is the virtue of the qín,
Unfathomable!
Its essence is pure, its spirit is distant,
So remote, it is difficult to reach!
Fine material and skilled hands,
Have met in this era!
In profuse and harmonious resonance,
It surpasses all other arts!
Those who understand music are few,
Who can truly treasure it?
Able to fully master the refined qín,
Are only the most virtuous people!
Pān Ānrén's Shēng Rhapsody
Among the treasures of the Hé and Fén rivers,

As for the continuous and abundant beauty of its spreading form,
the nourishment of its soaking spiritual liquid,
the configurations of its corners, bends, smooth and rugged,
and the joy of birds flying and gathering,
Because many authors have already detailed it,
I can afford to be brief.
Merely observing its instrument making,
one examines the thickness and thinness,
the shortness and length of the surfaces.
(They) arrange the growing reeds,
cut the ripe reeds.
(They) set the gong tone, differentiate the yu tones,

Releasing them reverses to quiet,
pressing them down then elevates.
The pipes are collected and arranged,
the sounds are essential and contain purity.
Each guards one and responds,

Establishing the huáng zhōng (standard pitch) to raise the tone,

Copying the imperial wings to insert feathers,

Like birds standing on tiptoe,

Side by side, scattered,

Thus, there is a beginning of prosperity and an end of frugality,

Urgent, sharp, and subtly pressing,

As for when the spring sun is just beginning to warm,
seeing off a departing friend beside the river,
the drinking at its height, the company rowdy,

and the host is slightly weary,

Then, at the end of the banquet,
he takes his friends by the hand.
Relaxing his stern expression,
he draws out hidden feelings.

We pour from bluish-white porcelain to serve Líng wine.
The radiant brilliance is solemnly and uniformly arrayed;
the pair of phoenixes sing in clamorous harmony.
Even musicians of Jìn respectfully abandon their zithers,

New sounds transform melodies,
and extraordinary tones overflow freely.
They entwine singing and drums,
and encompass bells and pitches.
They blaze brilliantly, releasing splendor;
they gather thickly and burst forth with energy.
"Autumn Wind" is sung on the roads of Yàn,

The largest note does not exceed the *gōng* tone,
and the smallest does not fall below the *yǔ* tone.
We sing forth "Zhāng" and "Xià",

They harmonize Chén and Sòng,

The near are not pressured, and the far are without separation;
the sounds form patterns, and the rhythms have order.
Government can have gains and losses,

and also how we change customs towards evil.
Therefore, though the instruments of strings and bamboo may not change,
the streams of *sāng* and *pú* have already arisen.
The *huáng* [reed pipe],
can refine the purity of all sounds.
The *shēng* [mouth organ],
can gather the forest of numerous purities.
The corrupt cannot find a place to put their wickedness,
the debauched cannot find a place to accommodate their licentiousness.
If it is not the harmonious music of the world,
the unchangeable virtuous sound,
who can participate in this?
A Rhapsody on Whistling by Chéng Gōngzǐ Ān
The eminent gentleman,
possesses a unique nature and loves the unusual.
He is disdainful of the world and forgets honor,
completely abandoning worldly affairs.
He looks up to the high and admires the ancient,
constantly engaging in distant thoughts.
He will ascend Mount Jī to assert his integrity,
and float on the vast sea to roam with his will.
Therefore, he invites friends,
and gathers like-minded people.
They delve into the ultimate secrets of nature and life,
and study the profound mysteries of morality.
Pitying the unenlightened of common customs,
he alone transcends and awakens first.
Finding the path of the world narrow and confined,
he looks up to the celestial road and steps high.
Distant from fine customs, he leaves behind the body,
Thereupon, he was filled with fervor and let out a long whistle.
At that time, the Yào Líng 曜靈 (sun) swiftly declined,
and the flowing light became dim over the Sì 汜 River.
Carefree, they held hands,
walking leisurely with measured steps.
They emitted wondrous sounds from their red lips,
and stirred mournful tones with their white teeth.
The sound, suppressed and raised, turned subtly,
and the energy, dense and agitated, flared up.
It harmonized the Huáng Gōng 黃宮 pitch with the Qīng Jiǎo 清角 mode,
and mingled the Shāng 羽 and Yǔ 羽 notes with the Liú Zhēng 流徵 mode.
It drifted through the clouds in the Tàiqīng 泰清 heavens,
and gathered long winds from ten thousand miles.
Once the melody ended, the resonance ceased,
yet the lingering delight remained unfinished.
It was truly the ultimate sound of nature,
not something that could be compared to string and bamboo instruments.
Therefore, the sound did not rely on instruments,
and its use did not borrow from objects.
It was taken from within the self,
employing the mind to control the breath.
Moving the lips created melodies,
and opening the mouth formed sounds.
Touching upon categories and moving objects,
they sang and chanted according to circumstance.
It was grand without being excessive,
and subtle without being submerged.
Its clarity is sharper than the *yúshēng* reed organ,
its gentle smoothness harmonizes with the *sèqín* zither.
Its profound mystery is sufficient to communicate with spirits and enlighten the soul,
its delicate subtlety is sufficient to explore the hidden and fathom the deep.
It restrains the lament and desolation of the "Jīchǔ,"
and tempers the extravagance and licentiousness of the "Běilǐ."
It relieves great floods during scorching droughts,
and reverses excessive *yáng* in deep *yīn*.
Its melodies lead to myriad changes,
its musical application is boundless.
It brings harmony and joy,
and crushes and conceals sorrow.
At times, it is secluded and scattered, about to cease,
at others, it is abruptly rousing and full of righteous indignation.
Slowly, it is gentle and leisurely,
rapidly, it is bustling and stirring.
When emotions are aroused, they can be reversed,
even though the heart is sad, it is not wounded.
It gathers the ultimate harmony of the eight tones,
and is truly supremely joyful without being unrestrained.
If one ascends a high terrace to gaze afar,
opens a decorated window to survey the landscape,
sighs with admiration, claps hands, and raises one's head,
drawing out long, loud, and clear sounds,
sometimes relaxing and reflecting on oneself,
sometimes pacing back and forth, then letting go,
sometimes gently and softly yielding,
Or rushing and surging with force.
Spreading, blocked, roaring and drying up,
Cold, drifting ethereally, clear and extended.
Unrestrained energy surges forth,
In a colorful and intricate interweaving.
Row upon row, swiftly rising,
Chirping and hissing, sounds are created.
It plays the long, drawn-out thoughts of the Hú horse,
Facing the cold wind towards the northern Shuo region.
It also resembles wild geese about to hatch their young,
A flock crying out in the desert.
Therefore, it can create sounds based on forms,
And make melodies according to events.
Responding to things without end,
The mechanism triggers, and the response is swift.
Oppressed and surging currents,
Intermingling discourses, clouds associated.
Seemingly separated, seemingly joined,
On the verge of ending, then resuming.
Fēi Lián beats within the dark tunnels,
And a fierce tiger responds in the central valley.
Nán Jī constellation moves in the vast sky,
And a clear gale shakes the tall trees.
It scatters stagnant accumulations and broadcasts them afar,
Washing away the murky turbidity of dust and haze.
It transforms the ultimate harmony of Yīn and Yáng,
And changes the obscene customs of excessive winds.
Ruò nǎi yóu Chónggāng,
ascends Jǐngshān.
Approaches the cliffside,
gazes at the flowing streams.
Sits upon the flat rocks,
rinses in the clear springs.
Leans on the pliant *gāolán* orchids,
sheltered by the coiling cicadas on the tall bamboo.
Then one sings and expresses,
sounds echoing one after another.
Unfolds the pent-up thoughts of melancholy,
releases the long-knotted entanglements.
The heart is cleansed and without burden,
the will departs from the mundane and floats freely.
As for imitating the sounds of metal and leather (instruments),
comparing to clay and gourd (instruments).
Many voices perform together,
like the *jiā* reed pipe and the *xiāo* flute.
Thundering and rumbling,
booming and clamorous.
When *zhǐ* (徵) is sounded, then deep winter produces warm vapor,
when *yǔ* (羽) is played, then severe frost causes summer to wither.
When *shāng* (商) is moved, then autumn rain descends in spring,
when *jué* (角) is played, then the valley wind sounds in the branches.
The pitch is not constant,
the melody has no fixed form.
Moving without drifting,
It stops without stagnating.
It develops and spreads following the articulation,
borrowing fragrant air to travel far away.
Its tone is subtle and its resonance flows,
its sound is intense and clear.
Truly, it is the ultimate beauty of nature,
surpassing the extraordinary and being unmatched in the world.
It surpasses the Sháo Xià (韶夏) and Xián Chí (咸池) melodies,
how can it merely seek to differ from the music of Zhèng (鄭) and Wèi (衛)?
At this time, Mián Jū (緜駒) was tongue-tied and lost his spirit,
Wáng Bào (王豹) kept his mouth shut and lost his color.
Yú Gōng (虞公) stopped his voice and ceased singing,
Níng Zǐ (甯子) restrained his hands and sighed.
Zhōng Qī (鍾期) abandoned his qín (琴) and changed to listening,
Kǒng Fù (孔父) forgot the taste and did not eat.
All the beasts danced and stamped their feet,
the phoenixes came in ceremony and flapped their wings.
Then one knows the wonder of the long whistle,
that indeed it is the ultimate of sounds and tones.
Suddenly changing its appearance,
in a very short time,
the transformations are endless.
The King asked Yù, saying:
"What is this vapor?"
Yù replied, saying:
"This is what is called 'Morning Cloud'."
The King said:
"What is meant by 'Morning Cloud'?"
Yù said:
"In the past, the former king once traveled to Gāotáng,
and, tired, he took a nap in the daytime.
He dreamt of seeing a woman who said:
'I am a daughter of Wūshān,
and a guest of Gāotáng.
I heard that you, my lord, are visiting Gāotáng,
and I wish to offer you my pillow and mat.'
The King then favored her.
Upon departing, she bid farewell, saying:
'I am on the sunny side of Wūshān,
blocked by high hills;
in the morning, I am the morning cloud,
and in the evening, I am the passing rain.
Morning after morning, evening after evening,
beneath the Yángtái terrace.'
The next morning he looked,
and it was as she said.
Therefore, he built a temple for her,
It was named
"Cháo Yún" (Morning Cloud).
The King said:
"When Morning Cloud first appears,
what is its appearance like?"
Yù (玉) replied:
"When it first appears,
it is bright and radiant, resembling a pine tree.
As it advances a little,
it is luminous and fair, like a beautiful woman.
Raising its sleeves to block the sun,
looking towards the one it longs for.
Suddenly it changes its appearance,
swift and powerful, like a team of four horses pulling a carriage,
with feathered banners erected.
It becomes somber, like the wind,
bleak, like the rain.
When the wind stops and the rain clears,
the cloud has no fixed place."
The King said:
"Can I now take a journey?"
Yù said:
"You can."
The King said:
"What will it be like?"
Yù said:
"It will be high and manifest,
allowing you to gaze afar!
Broad and vast,
the ancestor of all things!
Above, it reaches to the heavens;
below, it appears in the depths.
Precious, strange, wondrous, and grand,
beyond description or discussion."
The king said:
"Try to compose a rhapsody about it for me."
Yù said:
"Yes, yes."
Oh, the grand form of Gāo Táng,
truly there is nothing like it to compare.
Wū Shān is dazzling and boundless,
its paths twist and pile up layer upon layer.
Climbing the precipitous cliffs and looking down,
I overlook the vast embankment storing water.
Encountering the fresh clearing after a heavenly rain,
I observe the gathering of all the valleys.
Rushing and surging without a sound,
dissolving gently and entering together.
Spreading out in vast abundance in all directions,
thickly and deeply, it never stops.
The long wind arrives and the waves rise,
like a solitary acre on Mount Lí.
Its force strikes the shore against each other,
narrowing and drawing back to meet.
Towering angrily in the middle, especially high,
It is like floating on the sea and gazing at Mount Jiéshí.
The pebbles grind against each other with a rumbling sound,
and the shaking of the heavens is like a crashing, rumbling sound.
The huge rocks are submerged and babbling,
and the foam gushes and rises high.
The water is vast and meandering,
and the great waves surge and blend together.
They rush, rise, and strike against each other,
and the clouds rise with a sound of abundance.
Wild beasts are startled and leap in fear,
rushing about aimlessly and fleeing.
Tigers, leopards, wolves, and rhinoceroses,
lose their breath and are terrified.
Eagles, ospreys, hawks, and falcons,
fly up and down, hide and flee,
their legs tremble and they hold their breath,
how dare they rashly seize prey?
Thereupon, the water creatures are all exposed,
basking on the sunny banks.
Turtles, alligators, sturgeon, and great sturgeon,
pile up in a jumbled mess.
Flapping their scales and wings,
they writhe and coil.
Looking from afar on the middle slopes,
a dark tree blooms in winter.
Bright and shimmering,
it steals the brilliance from people's eyes.
Gleaming like scattered stars,
Their forms cannot be fully exhausted.
The hazel forest is lush and flourishing,
With petals and flowers covering all.
Twin branches hang down like rooms,
Entangled branches intertwine and meet.
Delicate and gentle,
Following the waves, obscure and dim.
Spreading wings east and west,
Curving and abundant.
Green leaves with purple inside,
Red stems with white calyxes.
Slender branches sadly moan,
The sound resembles reed pipes.
Clear and turbid harmonize,
Five changes and four gatherings.
Affecting the heart and moving the ears,
Twisting the intestines and wounding the spirit.
Lonely children and widowed women,
Hearts chilled and noses stinging with sorrow.
Petty officials abandon their posts,
Worthy scholars lose their ambition.
Sorrowful thoughts are endless,
Sighs and tears fall.
Climbing high and gazing afar,
It makes people's hearts weary.
Coiled banks are towering and imposing,
Repeated arrangements of mats.
The bedrock is treacherous and steep,
Sloping cliffs crumble.
The craggy rocks are uneven,
Running after each other horizontally and vertically.
Corners intersect in contradiction,
Caves on the back, lying down and treading.
Intertwined and accumulated,
Overlapping and increasing.
Resembling a pillar of rock,
Below Mount Wū.
Looking up at the mountaintop,
How dense and numerous it is,
The rainbow gleams and dazzles.
Looking down at the towering peaks,
Deep hollows are quiet and dark.
The bottom cannot be seen,
Only the sound of pines is heard.
The sloping banks are vast,
Standing and acting like a bear.
Staying for a long time without leaving,
Sweat pours from my feet.
Distant and vague,
Disappointed and lost.
It stirs the heart,
Causing inexplicable fear.
Even the decisiveness of Bēn Yù
Cannot summon courage.
Suddenly encountering a strange object,
not knowing where it came from.
Luxuriant and abundant,
as if born of ghosts,
as if emanating from spirits.
Its form resembles a running beast,
or perhaps resembles a flying bird.
Deceptive and strange, extraordinary and grand,
impossible to fully describe.
Above, it reaches the side of the observatory,
below, it covers the flat ground.
Spreading out from its base,
fragrant grasses grow everywhere.
Autumn orchids, zhǐ and huì,
and Jiānglí are lush and flourishing.
Blue quán and shègān,
and jiēchē shoots grow together.
The sparse grasses are delicate,
connected and stretching gracefully.
Yuè fragrance is dense and pervasive,
many birds chirp loudly.
Males and females are separated,
sadly crying out to one another.
Wángzū (osprey), líhuáng (oriole),
and the late Chǔ dove.
"Elder sister return" (a bird call) reminds the longing wife,
the "drooping chicken" (another bird call) is high in the nest.
Their cries are harmonious,
In those years, we roamed and travelled.
We sang and harmonized in turn,
following the tune and flowing with the stream.
There were men with methods,
Xiàn Mén Gāo Xī.
Ascending to become the Yù Forest,
where dukes rejoiced and gathered grains.
They presented pure sacrificial animals,
and prayed in the dark chamber.
They offered sacrifices to the various gods,
and paid homage to the Great One (Tài Yī).
The transmitted prayers were all prepared,
and the words were all completed.
The king then mounted the jade carriage,
drawn by four dark-green dragons.
The banners with tassels were hung,
and the pennants harmonized.
Thick strings were plucked, and elegant music flowed,
as the cold wind passed, increasing sorrow.
Thereupon, songs were sung,
causing people to feel grieved, despondent, and distressed,
holding their breath and sighing more.
Then the hunters were released,
their footprints like stars.
It was said that this was a feathered hunt,
with mouthpieces held, silent.
Bows and crossbows were not fired,
Fúmǐ (罘䍐) does not overturn.
Wading through the mǎngmǎng (漭漭),
galloping across the píngpíng (苹苹).
Flying birds have not yet risen,
running beasts have not yet darted forth.
Why such haste, so sudden,
hooves and feet sprinkled with blood?
Raising merit, gaining first,
the captured carts already full.
The king is about to go and see,
he must first purify and fast,
choosing the time and selecting the day.
Simple carriage, dark garments,
raising the yún pèi (雲斾),
a rainbow as the banner,
kingfisher feathers as the canopy.
The wind rises, the rain stops,
traversing a thousand *lǐ* in a flash.
The canopy is opened,
going to meet in person.
Thinking of all regions,
worrying about national harm.
Opening up to the wise and sage,
assisting those who are lacking.
Unblocking the nine orifices,
the spirit discerning stagnation.
Extending years, increasing longevity, a thousand ten thousand years.
Sòng Yù's Goddess Fù with Preface
King Xiāng of Chǔ and Sòng Yù were traveling along the shores of the Yúnmèng marshes,
and he ordered Yù to compose a fù concerning the affairs of Gāotáng.
That night, the king slept,
and indeed dreamed of encountering a goddess,
whose appearance was extremely beautiful.
The king was amazed by this,
and the next day,
told Yù about it.
Yù said,
"What was the dream like?"
The king said,
"After sunset,
my spirit became dazed and confused,
as if there was something to rejoice in.
In a flurry of confusion,
I did not know its meaning.
The appearance in my eyes was indistinct,
yet there were moments when I seemed to remember.
I saw a woman,
whose appearance was exceedingly strange and wonderful.
I dreamed of her while sleeping,
but upon waking, I did not recognize myself.
Distracted and unhappy,
I was forlorn and lost my purpose.
Thereupon, I calmed my heart and regulated my breath,
and again saw what I had dreamed."
The king said,
"What was her appearance like?"
Yù said,
"Abundant and beautiful!
All virtues were complete!
Magnificent and elegant!
Difficult to fathom and investigate completely!
Never before seen in ancient times,
Unseen by the world.
Extraordinary appearance and remarkable bearing,
Impossible to fully praise.
When she first arrived,
She shone like the newly risen sun illuminating the rafters.
As she moved forward slightly,
She was as bright as the clear moon spreading its light.
In a short time,
Beautiful features were born.
Gleaming like a flower,
Warm like jade.
The five colors appeared at once,
Impossible to fully describe.
Examining her closely,
She captivated one's eyes and essence.
When she was fully adorned,
Silks and brocades adorned with elaborate patterns,
Her extremely beautiful attire illuminated all directions.
She shook her embroidered robe,
And wore her skirt.
Neither too plump to be short,
Nor too slender to be long.
Her steps are graceful as she illuminates the halls.
Suddenly, her expression changes,
Supple as a dragon playing, riding the clouds and soaring.
Beautifully adorned with garments,
Elegantly wearing light makeup.
Bathed in orchid perfumes,
Holding fragrance like an orchid.
Her nature is harmonious and agreeable,
Suitable to attend by your side.
Deferential in order,
And well-tempered in heart."
The King said:
"How wonderful this is!
Try composing a *fù* for me about her."
Yù said:
"Yes, yes."
Oh, how beautiful is this goddess,
Endowed with the rich adornments of *yīn* and *yáng*.
Clothed in splendid ornaments so pleasing,
Like a kingfisher spreading its wings.
Her form is unparalleled,
Her beauty without limit.
Máo Qiáng covering her face with her sleeve,
Is not enough to compare to her.
Xī Shī veiling her face,
Compared to something colorless.
Up close, she is enchanting;
from afar, she inspires hope.
Her bone structure is remarkably unique,
a countenance befitting a ruler.
To look upon her fills the eyes;
who could surpass her in excellence?
In my heart, I am uniquely pleased,
my joy is boundless.
Our interactions are infrequent, and affection is distant,
making complete expression impossible.
Others cannot see her,
but the king observes her appearance.
Her appearance is lofty and majestic,
how can it be fully described?
Her appearance is full, abundant and with dignified grace,
enveloping a warm and lustrous jade-like face.
Her pupils are bright and clear,
revealing abundant beauty and captivating to behold.
Her eyebrows are delicate and arched like moths,
her vermillion lips are bright as cinnabar.
Her natural essence is rich and substantial,
her mind is at ease, and her body is relaxed.
She is both graceful and quiet in secluded stillness,
yet dances playfully among people.
She is suited for a high palace to expand her thoughts,
allowing for unrestrained and ample freedom.
Her silk skirts move like mist as she walks slowly,
The rustling sound of sweeping the steps.
She gazes at my curtain and stretches her eyes,
like the waves of a flowing stream about to surge.
She raises her long sleeves to adjust her lapel,
standing restlessly and pacing back and forth.
Serene and tranquil is her quiet grace,
her nature deep and thoughtful, not easily troubled.
At times she lingers with subtle movements,
her intentions yet to be fully understood.
Her thoughts seem near yet are already distant,
as if she will come but then retreats.
I lift my curtain and request her presence,
wishing to offer my sincere devotion.
She cherishes integrity and purity,
ultimately finding it difficult to agree with me.
She presents elegant words and offers her reply,
uttering fragrant phrases like orchids.
Our spirits engage in mutual exchange,
our hearts joyous and full of delight.
But our spirits remained alone and unfulfilled,
my soul forlorn and without end.
Containing her promises, not sharing them,
she sighs and raises her voice in lament.
With a hint of anger she restrains herself,
seemingly unapproachable and inviolable.
Thereupon, she shakes her jade ornaments,
The jade pendants chimed.
She straightened her clothes,
and composed her countenance.
She glanced at the female tutor,
and instructed the Grand Tutor.
Their joyous feelings were not yet joined,
and she was about to bid farewell and leave.
She lingered and drew back,
impossible to approach closely.
It seemed she would depart but did not,
inwardly appearing to turn her head.
Her eyes slightly glanced,
exchanging brilliant expressions.
Her will and demeanor were revealed freely,
impossible to fully record.
Her intention to leave was not decisive,
her spirit and heart filled with apprehension.
The rites were not completely performed,
the farewell words not fully spoken.
She wished for a brief moment,
but the goddess declared it urgent.
Her entrails twisted and her breath was injured,
confused and losing her composure.
Dimly and darkly, she became blind,
suddenly unaware of her location.
Her feelings she held privately,
with whom could she speak?
Sorrowfully she shed tears,
The search continued until dawn.
*Sòng Yù*'s and *Dēngtú Zǐ*'s "Rhapsody on Lust" with Preface
The grand master *Dēngtú Zǐ* was attending the King of *Chǔ*,
and he spoke ill of *Sòng Yù*, saying:
"*Sòng Yù* is a man of elegant appearance,
with many subtle words,
and he is also naturally lustful.
I hope that Your Majesty will not allow him to enter and exit the inner palace."
The King asked *Sòng Yù* about *Dēngtú Zǐ*'s words.
*Sòng Yù* replied:
"My elegant appearance
is what I received from Heaven;
my many subtle words
are what I learned from my teacher;
as for being lustful,
I do not have it."
The King said:
"If you are not lustful,
do you have an explanation?
If you have an explanation, then stay;
if you have no explanation, then leave."
*Sòng Yù* said:
"Among the beauties of the world, none are like those of the *Chǔ* kingdom;
among the beautiful women of the *Chǔ* kingdom, none are like those in my village;
among the beauties of my village, none are like the daughter of the family east of my house.
The daughter of the family east of my house,
if you add an inch, she would be too tall;
If diminished by even a fraction, it would be too short;
if powdered, it would be too white;
if rouged, it would be too red.
Her eyebrows are like the feathers of a kingfisher;
her skin is like white snow;
her waist is like bound silk;
her teeth are like shells held in the mouth.
A charming smile,
captivated Yángchéng,
and entranced Xiàcài.
Yet this woman has been peeking over the wall at me for three years,
and still she has not given her consent.
Dēngtú Zǐ, however, is not like that.
His wife has disheveled hair and twisted ears,
protruding lips and uneven teeth.
She walks sideways, limping,
and is afflicted with both scabies and hemorrhoids.
Dēngtú Zǐ delights in her
and has had five children with her.
Your Majesty, who can discern
who is truly the lecherous one?"
At this time, the Qin minister Zhāng Huá was at his side,
and so he stepped forward and said,
"Now, Sòng Yù greatly praises the woman next door,
considering her a beauty,
which is foolish and deluded!
I consider myself to uphold virtue,
and I believe that he is not as good as I am.
Furthermore, what could a concubine from a humble alley in Southern Chǔ [Chǔ] possibly say to Your Majesty?
As for my own insignificance,
what I have seen with my own eyes,
I dare not speak of it."
The King said,
"Try speaking of it for the sake of this humble one."
The Grand Master said,
"Yes, yes."
"When I was young, I once traveled far,
surveying the nine regions,
my feet traversed the five capitals.
I went out from Xiányáng [咸陽],
visited Hándān [邯鄲].
Leisurely, I was among the Zhèng [鄭] and Wèi [衛] regions, between the Zhēn [溱] and Wěi [洧] rivers.
It was then the end of spring,
welcoming the sun of summer.
The oriole birds chirped harmoniously,
groups of girls came out to pick mulberry leaves.
These beauties of the countryside,
their radiant complexions held a glow.
Their forms were beautiful and charming,
requiring no adornment.
I observed their loveliness,
and then recited a poem, saying:
'Following the great road, I grasp your sleeve,'
I presented them with fragrant flowers, the words exceedingly beautiful.
Thereupon, the maiden seemed as if she was expected but did not come,
and suddenly as if she had come but was not seen.
Her intention was close, but her body distant.
Looking down and up, the views were different.
She held back joy and smiled faintly,
secretly glancing with flowing eyes.
She then recited a poem, saying:
"Awakened by the spring breeze, fresh glory bursts forth.
I purify my chamber and await your kind voice and sound.
To give me this much is worse than not being born."
Consequently, she delayed and declined,
merely moving each other with subtle words,
their spirits relying on each other.
The eye desired her face,
the heart regarded her righteousness.
She upheld the poem and guarded propriety,
never going too far,
therefore, she was worthy of praise."
Thereupon, the King of Chǔ praised it as good,
and Sòng Yù consequently did not withdraw.
Cáo Zǐjiàn's Ode to the Luo River Goddess, with Preface
In the third year of the Huángchū era,
I paid court in the capital,
and on my return, I crossed the Luò River.
The ancients have said
that the spirit of this river
Named Mì Fēi.
Moved by Sòng Yù's account of the goddess to the King of Chǔ,
I then composed this *fù*.
The text reads:
I departed from the capital region, returning to my eastern fief.
With Yī Quē behind me,
I crossed Huán Yuán.
Passing through Tōng Gǔ,
climbing Jǐng Shān.
The sun having already declined in the west,
the carriage was weary, the horses exhausted.
Thereupon, I rested the carriage in the Héng marsh,
and pastured the team in the Zhī fields.
I strolled leisurely in the Yáng forest,
and cast my gaze along the Luò River.
At this, my essence shifted, my spirit startled,
and suddenly my thoughts scattered.
Looking down, I perceived nothing special,
but looking up, I saw a unique sight.
I beheld a beautiful woman,
beside a rocky bank.
Then I beckoned the driver and said to him:
"Have you seen her over there?
Who is that person,
so beautiful?"
The driver replied:
"I have heard of the goddess of the Hé and Luò rivers,
Her name is Mì Fēi.
Could it be that what the king saw,
was indeed her?
What is her appearance like?
Your subject wishes to hear of it."
I told him, saying:
"Her form,
is like a startled swan goose in flight,
graceful as a swimming dragon.
Radiant as the autumn chrysanthemum,
flourishing as the spring pine.
Faintly, she resembles light clouds veiling the moon,
drifting like swirling snow in flowing wind.
Seen from afar,
she is radiant as the sun rising in morning clouds;
examined up close,
she is bright as a lotus emerging from clear waves.
Plumpness and slenderness are perfectly balanced,
tallness and shortness are in perfect proportion.
Her shoulders are as if carved,
her waist is like bound white silk.
A long, graceful neck and fair nape,
reveal a pure, white complexion.
Fragrant gloss needs no adding,
and powder and rouge are not employed.
Her cloud-like hair is piled high,
her long eyebrows are delicately arched.
Her vermilion lips were bright and clear,
her glistening white teeth shone within.
Her bright eyes knew how to glance invitingly,
her dimples supported the power of her cheekbones.
Her extraordinary beauty was elegant and unrestrained,
her deportment was serene, her body relaxed.
Her tender feelings were conveyed with grace,
more charming than words could express.
Her unique attire transcended the age,
her bone structure matched the painted image.
She wore shimmering silk robes,
and jade ornaments of brilliant jasper adorned her ears.
She wore golden and emerald headdresses,
and luminous pearls were fastened to illuminate her form.
She trod in embroidered shoes for distant travels,
and trailed light skirts of misty silk gauze.
The faint fragrance of hidden orchids emanated,
as she walked hesitantly at the corner of the mountain.
"Then suddenly she let loose her body,
to roam and play.
On the left, she leaned on colorful feathered staffs,
on the right, she was shaded by cinnamon banners.
She bared her white wrists at the riverbank of the gods,
and gathered dark fungi from the swift currents.
My feelings were delighted by her virtuous beauty,
my heart fluttered and was not at peace.
Without a good matchmaker to arrange our joy,
Entrusting subtle ripples to convey my words.
I wish my sincere feelings would reach her first,
And I loosen the jade pendant to beckon her.
Alas! That beauty is truly virtuous,
For she is well-versed in etiquette and understands poetry.
She raises the beautiful jade to harmonize with me,
And points to the deep abyss as our appointed time.
Holding onto sincere and earnest affections,
I fear that this spirit might deceive me.
Recalling Jiāo Fǔ 交甫 breaking his promise,
I am filled with melancholy and hesitation.
Composing my countenance and calming my mind,
I reinforce the boundaries of propriety to restrain myself.
"Thereupon, the Lòu River 洛河 spirit was moved,
Wandering and hesitating.
The divine light flickered,
Sometimes dim, sometimes bright.
She raises her light body like a crane standing,
As if about to fly but not yet soaring.
She treads upon the fragrant path of peppercorns,
And walks through the thicket of *héng* leaves, spreading fragrance.
She utters a long sigh of enduring longing,
Her voice sorrowful and increasingly drawn out.
"Then, many spirits gathered in a throng,
Calling companions and gathering friends.
Some play in the clear stream,
Some soared over divine islands;
some gathered bright pearls,
